Article Title: 'Distressing': BJP slams Congress over three of its CMs 'skipping' Brics dinner
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party on Tuesday slammed Congress after three of its chief ministers skipped the dinner for Brics leaders hosted by the government, accusing them of "prioritising partisan politics over the national interest. "At a press conference, BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj asked Congress whether, in opposing Prime Minister Narendra Modi, it had begun opposing India as well."Political and ideological differences can always exist in politics. But when it comes to India and national interest, there should be no room for personal animosity or discord," Bansuri said."It is distressing that when the three chief ministers from the Congress party were invited to the Brics summit dinner, they prioritised partisan politics over the national interest .... I would like to ask Congress - in your opposition to PM Modi, have you now started to oppose India as well?" she added.BJP MP's remarks came after official sources said that CMs hailing from opposition parties were also invited for Brics dinner but did not attend the event.While Tamil Nadu CM Vijay was abroad, three Congress CMs invited for the dinner chose to skip it.A day before the dinner on September 12, Telangana CM Revanth Reddy had accepted the invitation for the dinner hosted by PM Modi.However, Reddy's office later conveyed to govt that he would be unable to attend due to "unavoidable circumstances".Two other Congress chief ministers, V D Satheesan of Kerala and D K Shivakumar of Karnataka, also skipped the dinner.The decision to invite CMs of different states for the dinner for BRICS leaders was in keeping with govt's move to host numerous events related to the grouping during India's presidency across various cities, and the decision of opposition CMs to skip it was unfortunate, the sources said.
Article Summary: Bjp mp bansuri swaraj asked congress whether, in opposing prime minister narendra modi, it had begun opposing india as well. While tamil nadu cm vijay was abroad, three congress cms invited for the dinner chose to skip it.

Article Title: West Bengal: BJP fields slain Suvendu Adhikari aide's mother for Nandigram bypoll
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party on Tuesday fielded Hansirani Rath, mother of CM Suvendu Adhikari’s late personal assistant Chandranath Rath, from the Nandigram assembly seat for the bypoll.Chandranath was shot dead in West Bengal's Madhyamgram two days before Suvendu took oath as chief minister.Suvendu visited the family shortly after, assuring them he would act as their household guardian.Meanwhile, Hansirani is also a five-term panchayat and panchayat samiti poll winner.The Nandigram seat in Purba Medinipur district was vacated by Adhikari, who retained Bhabanipur after winning both constituencies in the assembly elections. BJP also nominated Sarkar from the Rejinagar assembly constituency for the October 6 bypolls. Sarkar is a former BJP president of Murshidabad district and a member of the party's state committee.The Rejinagar assembly constituency in Murshidabad district was vacated by Aam Janata Unnayan Party founder Humayun Kabir, who had also won from Nowda.On Sunday, the Trinamool Congress announced Sanchita Pradhan (Dey) as its candidate for Nandigram and Rabiul Alam Chowdhury for Rejinagar in the upcoming by-elections.The party made the announcement in a post on X, saying the candidates were being announced under the guidance and inspiration of its chairperson and former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee."All India Trinamool Congress, under the guidance and inspiration of our Hon’ble Chairperson Smt @MamataOfficial, is pleased to announce the candidates for the upcoming Nandigram & Rejinagar by-elections. We wish Smt Sanchita Pradhan (Dey) and Shri Rabiul Alam Chowdhury the very best for this journey. May they carry forward the hopes and aspirations of the people with strength and determination," the party said in the post.From Congress, Mohd. Abdullahil Kafi will contest from Rejinagar assembly constituency, while Milan Pradhan has been named the candidate from Nandigram.
Article Summary: Hansirani rath, mother of cm suvendu adhikari’s late personal assistant chandranath rath, is fielded for the nandigram assembly seat. Rath is also a five-term panchayat and panchaysat samiti poll winner. The trinamool congress announced sanchita pradhan (dey) and rabiul alam chowdhury for rejinagar on sunday.

Article Title: Delhi to hold month-long Seva Sankalp Abhiyan from September 17, projects worth Rs 13,820 crore lined up
Article Text:
Delhi to hold month-long Seva Sankalp Abhiyan from September 17, projects worth ₹13,820 crore lined up

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Delhi government will launch a month-long public service campaign, the 'Seva Sankalp Abhiyan', from September 17 to October 17 to mark Prime Minister Narendra Modi's birthday, Chief Minister Rekha Gupta announced on Monday.The campaign will see government departments roll out a range of public welfare activities, including blood donation drives, health camps for senior citizens, worker registration, cleanliness campaigns and plantation programmes. Development projects worth around ₹13,820 crore are also scheduled to be inaugurated or have their foundation stones laid during the month-long campaign.Addressing a press conference at the BJP state office, Gupta said the initiative was intended to turn the Prime Minister's birthday into a month of public service and outreach.She said the spirit of service should remain at the centre of governance and that government power should be used as a means to serve citizens rather than as a privilege.The campaign will begin on September 17 with a mega blood donation camp organised by the Health Department. The government has set a target of collecting 2,500 units of blood in a single day.Health check-up camps will also be organised for around 25,000 senior citizens across Delhi, with the Health and Social Welfare departments working together on the initiative.The Labour Department will conduct registration and health check-ups for workers and construction workers during the campaign. The government said the registration exercise would help eligible workers access welfare schemes and other government services.A major initiative under the campaign will be the launch of Delhi's State Organ and Tissue Transplant Organisation (SOTTO) platform.According to the Chief Minister, the platform has been developed along the lines of the system operated by the Central government and will be used to spread awareness about organ donation and encourage more people to register as donors. The Women and Child Development Department will also conduct welfare activities for children living in child care centres.The Yamuna will be a major focus of the campaign. Gupta said projects worth approximately ₹8,000 crore related to cleaning and rejuvenating the river would be inaugurated or have their foundation stones laid during the campaignThe government will also organise extensive cleanliness drives along the Yamuna and across Delhi's wards and Assembly constituencies. Under its 'Clean Delhi, Green Delhi' push, the Environment Department has set a target of planting 70 lakh trees and saplings. Plantation drives will be held in every ward as part of the month-long programme. Young people will also be brought into the campaign through the 'Mere Sapnon Ka Bharat' competition.Painting, speech and reel-making contests will be organised around the theme of the India that young people envision. The government expects around five lakh students from nearly 5,000 schools to participate.Students from Delhi government schools, private schools, municipal schools and New Delhi Municipal Council schools will be included, along with university students.On the evening of September 17, the government will organise the 'Aashirwad ka Diya' programme, under which beneficiaries across Delhi will light lamps at their homes to mark PM Modi's birthday and convey their greetings.Gupta said the programme was also intended to mark PM Modi's 25 years in public service, from his tenure as Gujarat Chief Minister to his current role as Prime Minister.Another initiative, 'Namo Seva Ki Ankahi Kahaniyan', will highlight the experiences of beneficiaries whose lives have been positively affected by government schemes. Their stories will be documented and presented to the public through videos and street plays.The campaign will also recognise Delhi's anganwadi workforce. The Chief Minister said all anganwadi workers would be felicitated under the 'Aangan Ka Milan' programme.Delhi has 10,897 anganwadi centres and around 21,350 anganwadi workers, according to the government. A 'Seva Jyoti Kalash Yatra' will also be organised, with public representatives participating alongside citizens. One of the campaign's key outreach programmes will be the 'Seva Setu Abhiyan', under which three-day camps will be organised in all 70 Assembly constituencies.Officials from different departments will be available at these camps to explain Central and Delhi government schemes, assist eligible residents with registrations and help people access government services.The government will also organise 'Sushasan Seva Samvad' sessions, giving residents an opportunity to interact directly with officials and learn about ongoing projects, schemes and governance initiatives.The campaign will include an 'Innovation Challenge' aimed at giving young innovators a platform to showcase their ideas. Delhi is among five centres selected nationally for the initiative, and participants from neighbouring states will also be connected with the Delhi centre.Under 'Seva Ke Rang, Rashtra Ke Sang', rangoli and mandala art activities will be organised around themes of national unity, education and environmental protection. A large human rangoli involving thousands of participants is also being planned.Beyond the welfare programmes, the government plans to use the campaign to showcase its development agenda. Gupta said projects across different Delhi government departments, with a combined value of approximately ₹13,820 crore, would be inaugurated or have their foundation stones laid during the month.She also highlighted infrastructure projects undertaken in Delhi and the surrounding region during PM Modi's tenure, including the Delhi-Meerut Expressway, Delhi-Dehradun Expressway, Delhi-Mumbai Expressway, Dwarka Expressway, UER-2 and the Eastern and Western Peripheral Expressways.According to Gupta, the total value of infrastructure projects approved, under implementation or proposed for Delhi during the Prime Minister's tenure stands at around ₹12.25 lakh crore.She also pointed to projects including Jewar Airport, the Regional Rapid Transit System, Delhi Metro expansion and the signal-free corridor at Dhaula Kuan, as well as venues such as Yashobhoomi and Bharat Mandapam.Gupta said the infrastructure expansion had strengthened Delhi's connectivity and helped the capital host major international events, including the recently held 18th BRICS Summit.Concluding her address, the Chief Minister extended birthday wishes to PM Modi and said she hoped he would remain healthy and continue serving the country. (ANI)
Article Summary: Delhi to hold month-long seva sankalp abhiyan from september 17, projects worth ₹13,820 crore lined up. Chief minister rekha gupta said the initiative was intended to turn the prime minister's birthday into a month of public service. The campaign will include an 'innovation challenge' aimed at giving young innovators a platform to showcase their ideas.

Article Title: Yogi Adityanath announces welfare measures, tech push for lawyers in UP
Article Text:
Uttar Pradesh CM Yogi Adityanath

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

PRAYAGRAJ: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Monday took a swipe at the previous Samajwadi Party government, saying that before 2017, the state faced not only a shortage of resources but also issues related to governance, transparency, accountability, law and order, and judicial infrastructure.Additionally, the chief minister revealed plans to provide tablets to 400 state law officers to equip them with modern technology, enabling them to access information on government-related cases before the courts.In another announcement, Adityanath said the state government would introduce a cashless insurance scheme providing coverage of up to Rs 5 lakh for practising advocates in Uttar Pradesh.Addressing a felicitation ceremony organised by the Allahabad High Court Bar Association here, Adityanath said nearly 45 to 50 per cent posts in the Uttar Pradesh Police were vacant before his government assumed office in 2017."Before 2017, the challenge before us was not merely of resources. It was also a challenge of the system and approach, transparency and accountability in administration, law and order and judicial infrastructure," the chief minister said.He highlighted that the police force's annual training capacity at that time was only about 3,000 personnel but has now increased to 60,000."There was no training capacity and even basic facilities for the police were lacking," Adityanath said, adding that his government has strengthened police infrastructure and training facilities across the state.Adityanath also addressed the condition of the subordinate judiciary before 2017, pointing out that many courts operated in dilapidated or temporary buildings, and that district courts in as many as ten districts functioned from rented premises.Furthermore, he stated that his government had also addressed several shortcomings that earlier hampered the criminal justice system, including witnesses turning hostile out of fear in serious criminal cases and inadequate arrangements for transporting prisoners from jails to courts."Today, you can see the results of better coordination between the executive and the judiciary. When we reform and transform, the performance becomes visible on its own," the chief minister said.He emphasised that a robust judiciary strengthens the foundations of good governance, which should be the top priority of any elected government.Adityanath noted hat his government has prioritised greater use of technology, modernised infrastructure, and improved coordination between police and prosecution, leading to significant increases in conviction rates.He pointed out that the prosecution system is now connected to online platforms to ensure timely charge sheet filings and effective presentations of scientific evidence in court.Referring to emerging challenges, Adityanath said the legal fraternity must prepare itself for areas ranging from cybercrime and artificial intelligence to data privacy, e-commerce, fintech, intellectual property and climate litigation."A future-ready Bar will lay a strong foundation for a future-ready justice system," he said, adding that the younger generation of lawyers has a major responsibility in carrying forward the rich traditions of the Allahabad High Court.The chief minister said that district courts and jails have been provided with high-speed internet and video conferencing facilities. Additionally, the virtual recording of evidence and the digitization of court documents are being promoted to reduce trial delays."Justice delayed is justice denied," he said, stressing that timely and impartial justice was essential to maintaining public faith in the judiciary and other democratic institutions.Integrated court complexes were being developed to provide judicial facilities, residential accommodation for judicial officers, chambers for lawyers and other amenities under one roof, he said.Moreover, he outlined welfare measures for advocates, announcing that financial assistance from the lawyers' welfare fund has increased from Rs 1.5 lakh to Rs 5 lakh. The age limit for financial assistance to the families of deceased advocates has also been raised from 60 to 70 years.Adityanath said a strong judiciary forms the foundation of good governance and called for continued coordination and mutual respect between the Bar and the Bench."Only a future-ready Bar can lay a strong foundation for a future-ready justice system," he said.Adityanath announced that the state government would fully support the provision of essential facilities, including furniture and equipment, for the chambers constructed for over 10,000 lawyers as part of the multi-level parking and chamber complex.He stated that the government would assist in receiving proposals through the judiciary and the chief justice. PTI
Article Summary: Uttar pradesh chief minister yogi adityanath took a swipe at the previous samajwadi party government. He said the state faced not only a shortage of resources but also issues related to governance, transparency, accountability, law and order, and judicial infrastructure.

Article Title: 'Tareekh Pe Tareekh': 100% complete, still no keys - Inside RERA’s extension loop
Article Text:
File Image

tareekh pe tareekh.

When the percentage does not tell the whole story

The project that was 97% complete in 2020

The Main Issues

Extensions are a large part of the system

When 100% still isn't possession

What happens when another deadline is needed?

The law allows more than one route

The database which is needed

FPCE view

A housing project misses its promised completion date. The developer asks for more time. The regulator grants it. There is nothing extraordinary about that sequence. Construction can be held up for many reasons, some of them outside a developer's control. Sometimes a few more months are exactly what a project needs to get buyers their homes. The difficulty begins when the wait becomesThe question is simple. When a delayed project is given more time, how often does that extra time actually result in completion? There is no national public number that answers it.TOI tried to get closer to one by examining Maharashtra, one of the country's largest RERA (Real Estate Regulatory Authority) markets. It analysed 4,237 registrations appearing on MahaRERA's list of projects kept in abeyance after their completion dates had lapsed, as the list stood on Sept 10, 2026. A public reconstruction of MahaRERA filings by ReraGenie was used to identify projects with recorded extension histories. TOI then checked all 110 that the reconstruction showed with at least three recorded extension-history events against MahaRERA's own records.The reconstruction identified 1,154 of the 4,237, or 27.2%, with at least one recorded extension-history event. There were 392 with two or more and 110 with three or more. The 27.2% is not a failure rate. These projects were already on a lapse-related abeyance list, and abeyance is an administrative status. MahaRERA says projects on its lapse-related abeyance list have their bank accounts frozen, while promoters are prohibited from executing agreements for sale or sale deeds until the required compliances are fulfilled.Not every extension-history event represents a new deadline either. More than one filing can relate to the same revised date. What the exercise does establish is how often the completion clock can keep running long after the original date has passed.Abhay Upadhyay, president of the Forum for People's Collective Efforts (FPCE), a homebuyers' body that has examined the use of extensions across several states, argues that the statute is not where the problem lies. He says, "RERA is watertight, what has gone wrong is the practice built around it." The force majeure route under Section 6, in his view, has come to be treated almost as a given, with promoters approaching the regulator confident that an extension will follow.Often numbers can flatter to deceive. Take Indraprasthanagari Phase 1 in Pune. MahaRERA was told in one extension filing that the project was 98% complete. In another it was 95%. In a later filing it was back to 98%, while the revised completion date moved from December 2022 to May 2023 and then June 2024. An engineer's certificate in January 2023 put the project cost at ₹16.62 crore, with ₹1.66 crore still to be spent. An architect's certificate from the same period put key finishing and services work at 80% in Building A and 90% in Buildings B and C; the same figures appeared a year later.The same gap between a headline completion number and the documents underneath it appears in FPCE's 192-page report on project extensions. The report describes its cases as samples, not a census.In one Karnataka project, an April 2024 regulatory order recorded the project as 94% complete . A later order cited completion at 76%, relying on progress information that was more than two years old.Upadhyay's objection is to the sequence. "As soon as a promoter wants an extension, they should be asked the hard question, in the first instance only," he says. In Uttar Pradesh, he says, the report found instances where UPRERA granted extensions and carried out site visits afterwards.Gajanan Plaza in Mumbai's Borivali shows how long the gap between "almost complete" and delivery can stretch. In January 2020, its promoter told MahaRERA that 97% of the project had been completed onsite. Some buyers had been promised possession as far back as 2012.They had originally booked residential flats before the project was converted to commercial use. By July 2024, 11 complainants across seven units, who had paid a combined ₹1.67 crore, were still before MahaRERA seeking enforcement of orders in their favour.In one proceeding, the regulator recorded "intentional default" in complying with its earlier directions. Gajanan Plaza had originally been registered to finish on Dec 31, 2018. At a February 2025 hearing, the promoter sought time until December 2027, saying Phase 1 was almost complete but financially dependent on a proposed Phase 2.MahaRERA's live project page, as of September 2026, carries a revised completion date of April 30, 2028. The page states that the date includes the four-month extension granted under MahaRERA Order 66/2026, a blanket force majeure extension applied automatically to eligible projects across the state.MahaRERA's own annual figures give a sense of how much of its work is now extension work. In 2025-26, the regulator reported 4,204 fresh registrations, 2,488 corrections and 3,687 timeline extensions. That works out to nearly 88 extensions for every 100 fresh registrations. Extensions made up 35.5% of those three categories. That does not mean 88% of new projects were delayed. An extension granted in 2025-26 can relate to a project registered several years earlier.But the figures do indicate how much regulatory activity now involves projects whose original timelines have already changed. Keeping a registration alive can also matter commercially. In four of the 110 projects examined by TOI, promoters explicitly stated that an extension or extension number was needed to continue selling unsold flats.Among the 110 projects, TOI found at least 12 where a promoter filing described the project or overall construction as at least 95% complete while seeking more time. At least five explicitly claimed 100% completion. At least four made a 95%-plus claim in more than one filing.Shiv Sparsh Phase II is a case in point. Its promoter described the project as 100% complete in three extension filings while also stating that fire and lift NOCs were awaited. The revised deadlines eventually ran through July 2024. A March 2025 architect's certificate again put the main building-work categories at 100%. Its separate common-area entry for "Fire Protection & Fire Safety requirements" carried no completion percentage. At other projects, even the basic progress update may be missing. In May 2026, MahaRERA issued show-cause notices to 8,212 of 33,029 registered housing projects after they failed to file mandatory quarterly progress reports for the January-March quarter by the April 20 deadline.TOI also examined 10 MahaRERA orders issued in 2025 under Section 7(3), which allows the authority, instead of revoking a project's registration, to let it continue subject to conditions. All 10 recorded that the promoter had failed to obtain the 51% majority allottee consent referred to in MahaRERA's procedure. All 10 nevertheless granted further time. That is not, in itself, improper. Across the orders, though, the argument is substantially the same: refusing continuation could stop the project and harm buyers, and the "balance of convenience" therefore favours allowing it to proceed subject to conditions.Upadhyay says the pattern is not confined to Maharashtra. Extensions granted despite the absence of the 51% consent also turn up in FPCE's examination of orders across states.The Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act was passed in 2016 and came fully into force on May 1, 2017, after years of demands for a law to discipline a sector in which buyers had little recourse against delay. It is a central statute administered locally: each state and union territory frames its own rules and appoints its own authority. MahaRERA, which began work in 2017, is among the oldest and busiest.RERA does not contain a simple one-extension rule. Section 6 limits extensions granted under it to one year in aggregate. Section 7(3), separately, allows a regulator, instead of revoking registration, to keep it in force subject to conditions. MahaRERA has used this route in post-lapse continuation proceedings.In its 2017 Neelkamal Realtors judgment, the Bombay High Court held that continuation beyond the ordinary extension framework could be considered case by case in exceptional, compelling circumstances. For buyers, another clock runs alongside the regulatory one. Under Section 18, an allottee who stays in a delayed project is entitled to interest for every month of delay until possession. A buyer who withdraws can seek a refund with interest. Upadhyay points to Supreme Court rulings affirming that entitlement and says very little has changed on the ground.Even official estimates put the scale of housing stress high. A government-appointed committee headed by Amitabh Kant cited Indian Banks' Association estimates of around 4.12 lakh stressed dwelling units involving ₹4.08 lakh crore in legacy stalled projects. FPCE reaches a much larger figure: ₹12.44 lakh crore affecting around 27.6 lakh families, by its estimate. The figure is modelled, not a project-by-project count.India does have a count of registered RERA projects. When the Centre launched its Unified RERA Portal in September 2025, 1,51,113 projects had been registered nationally. At the same meeting, however, the government said a nationwide project database should still be prepared.And in March 2026, the housing ministry told Parliament that detailed state-level information sought by MPs was "not centrally maintained". However a publicly accessible national record linking the complete journey of a project is currently missing. Upadhyay says the gap is not for want of asking. The issue has been raised in central forums and instructions to furnish the data have been issued, he says, but the data has not followed.Section 8, which allows a project to be taken out of a promoter's hands, should be used far more often, Upadhyay argues, on the reasoning that the prospect of losing the project is what makes a developer move. By the time a project has lost its financial viability, action against the promoter achieves little. "What a RERA registration ought to carry is a definitive guarantee to the ordinary buyer," Upadhyay says.Ten years after RERA came into force, the unresolved question is no longer whether delayed projects sometimes need more time. It is how regulators decide when more time is still a solution, and when it has simply become another deadline.
Article Summary: Toi analysed 4,237 registrations appearing on maharera's list of projects kept in abeyance after their completion dates had lapsed. There were 392 with two or more extensions and 110 with three or more. The 27.2% is not a failure rate. Maharera's own annual figures give a sense of how much of its work is now extension work.

Article Title: Jethmalani: Why wasn't FIR slapped on Varma?
Article Text:
Justice Varma had on April 10 resigned as a judge of Allahabad High Court and had withdrawn from the inquiry proceedings

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Leading lawyers Harish Salve and Mahesh Jethmalani Monday advocated a reset in the judiciary, as happened after the Emergency, and said the complaint redressal mechanism needs to be reformed for the public to continue reposing faith in the institution.Referring to the unprecedented discovery of burning cash at Justice Yashwant Varma's residence in March last year, Jethmalani asked why an FIR was not registered given that the judge had repeatedly moved the SC seeking the quashing of the inquiry.Jethmalani said there is a dire need for the infusion of transparency in the working of the judiciary. Salve asked if a minister would have escaped an FIR if such an incident had happened at their residence. What would have been the judiciary's response to a PIL on such an incident being reported from the residence of a person who was not part of the judiciary.CJI Surya Kant, responding to the queries at the Ram Jethmalani Memorial Lecture, said the internal mechanism to deal with complaints against judges is robust, responsive, and expeditious."No doubt every system and mechanism can be improved. But I can assure you that the internal mechanism to deal with complaints against judges has been adequate," he said.CJI Kant said most of the complaints against judges are filed by disgruntled litigants after suffering a reversal in court."Would it be proper to adjudicate these complaints in the public domain? If so done, what happens to the judges and the judiciary?" the chief justice asked.Salve said the courts must stick to their field: the law."When they deviate from that, the results have been devastating. Court-monitored investigations are a myth. What happened in the 2G spectrum allocation scam, coal block allocation scam, and Hawala scam cases, investigations into which were monitored by courts? When the court monitors an investigation, the investigating agency loses its independence and feels obliged to deliver results, and that is when things get skewed," Salve said.He said a strong judiciary is welcome. "When it is strong at a time when govt is weak, everyone applauds it for raising questions. But when there is a strong govt, the public judges the judiciary on how often it raises questions before the govt. It is then that the balance between the three organs gets disturbed," he said.Jethmalani criticised the opaqueness in the appointments and transfers of judges in constitutional courts and said the area needs reforms to allay apprehensions of favouritism and nepotism.CJI Kant said the collegium system has evolved over the years, and the smooth manner in which the appointments and transfers take place in consultations with govt shows that there is little reason to doubt its efficacy.
Article Summary: Leading lawyers harish salve and mahesh jethmalani advocate a reset in the judiciary. They say the complaint redressal mechanism needs to be reformed for the public to continue reposing faith in the institution. Chief justice surya kant says the internal mechanism to deal with complaints against judges is robust, responsive, and expeditious.

Article Title: On Shah's UCC claim, 3 BJP allies sound caution
Article Text:
Amit Shah

Picking up pace

JDU, TDP have history of independent positions

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A day after Union home minister Amit Shah expressed confidence that 21 NDA-governed states would implement Uniform Civil Code by 2029, three BJP allies struck a circumspect note.Lavu Sri Krishna Devarayalu, parliamentary party leader of Telugu Desam Party which is in office in Andhra Pradesh, told TOI, "As of now, there is no discussion but whenever we find the need for it, we will look into it. We will definitely involve various stakeholders before we adopt it. "JD(U), which is part of the BJP-led coalition in Bihar, said it would speak with Shah. "I will meet home minister Amit Shah and discuss the issue," the party's working president Sanjay Jha told TOI.JD(U) chief Nitish Kumar, who stepped down as Bihar's longest-serving CM to make way for BJP's Samrat Chaudhary in April, had in the past supported the idea of UCC but emphasised that a consensus should be evolved by taking all communities on board.Another BJP ally, Chirag Paswan of Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas), also chose to be cautious, saying his party was committed to uniformity and diversity and the Constitution has acknowledged different traditions and practices of different communities. Exemptions for Scheduled Tribes under different schedules and articles of the Constitution were proof of this, he said.The proposal for UCC should be made public, interests of stakeholders considered and comprehensive consultation should follow, he said, adding that his party would make its stand clear after this.Both Telugu Desam Party and JD(U) have a history of taking independent positions on some of the key ideological planks of the BJP since 2014. Both have been in and out of the NDA during this period but are seen to be aligned more closely with the BJP in the third term of PM Narendra Modi. Despite being a BJP ally, JD(U) MPs had not voted in support of Article 370’s abrogation in Parliament in 2019 and had walked out.Addressing a press conference in Mumbai, Shah had said, “Triple talaq has been abolished, giving Muslim women equal rights. We have introduced Uniform Civil Code in several states and I am confident that in the 21 BJP-NDA ruled states, we will introduce UCC before 2029.”The next Lok Sabha polls are scheduled for 2029.BJP has gone for the rollout of UCC through states governed by it instead of its nationwide implementation in one go. It is already in force in Uttarakhand, while Gujarat, Assam and Madhya Pradesh have passed the law as well.
Article Summary: Home minister amit shah has expressed confidence that 21 nda-governed states would implement uniform civil code by 2029. But three bjp allies struck a circumspect note. Telugu desam party and jd(u) have a history of taking independent positions on some of the key ideological planks of the bjp since 2014.

Article Title: Ram temple trust rejects claim ex-Air Marshal Mishra skipped CEO interview round
Article Text:
Air Marshal (retd.) Jeetendra Mishra

NEW DELHI: Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshtera has refuted claims that retired Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra did not participate in the interview rounds of the selection process for the chief executive officer of Ram temple in Ayodhya.In a statement, trust's general secretary Swami Govind Dev Giri said that the search committee for the CEO conducted a multi-tier evaluation process involving AI-based screening and manual assessment across three cities, Delhi NCR, Pune and Sambalpur."The selection process was conducted in accordance with the highest standards of institutional governance and transparency. Article Title: Aaditya Thackeray, Rhea Chakraborty named in Disha Salian's death case: Key details from CBI FIR
Article Text:

Bombay HC orders CBI probe

NEW DELHI: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on Monday registered an FIR in connection with the death of Disha Salian, the former manager of late actor Sushant Singh Rajput, following an order of the Bombay high court.The FIR names several individuals whose roles have been listed for investigation, including Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray, Rohan Roy, actors Dino Morea and Sooraj Pancholi, Aaditya's bodyguards, Rhea Chakraborty , Showik Chakraborty, former police officer Sachin Vaze, former Mumbai police commissioner Param Bir Singh, DCP Vishal Thakur and former Maharashtra chief minister Uddhav Thackeray.The document also names former state home minister Anil Deshmukh, several police officers, forensic officials, doctors and other individuals.“The then chief minister Uddhav Thackeray, father of Aaditya Thackeray, and others also played a significant role in the conspiracy and subsequent cover-up. The concerned public servants and police officers are also liable to be investigated for destruction or suppression of case papers, files and other public records, fabrication of official records, and misuse of public funds, manpower and police machinery for unlawful purposes and for shielding the offenders,” the FIR stated.The FIR said the listed individuals would be investigated in connection with the alleged principal offences, criminal conspiracy, the “subsequent creation and propagation of the false suicide story” and the alleged suppression, destruction or fabrication of evidence.It also named officers associated with Malvani Police Station, doctors and staff involved in the post-mortem, officials of the Forensic Science Laboratory in Kalina, security guards of Regent Galaxy Building, members of the special investigation team and other unidentified persons.Earlier this month, the Bombay high court ordered a CBI investigation into Salian’s death and criticised the Mumbai Police for failing to register an FIR for six years.The court observed that the police investigation “raises more questions than answers”. The bench also questioned the decision to treat the case only as an accidental death and pointed to “glaring discrepancies” in the investigation.Salian died on June 8, 2020, after falling from a residential building in Mumbai’s Malad area. Mumbai Police had registered an Accidental Death Report (ADR) in the case.Salian had briefly worked as Sushant's manager. The actor was found dead at his Bandra residence on June 14, 2020, six days after Salian’s death.The proximity of the two deaths triggered widespread speculation about a possible link, although the cases were investigated separately.Following the public uproar over Rajput’s death, the Maharashtra government ordered a CBI probe. The agency later submitted a closure report stating that Rajput had died by suicide. The report, however, is yet to be heard by the court concerned.Earlier, Salian’s father, Satish Salian, had accused Aaditya Thackeray and actor Dino Morea in connection with his daughter’s death.Speaking to ANI on Friday, Satish Salian said he had told investigators what he knew about the events surrounding his daughter's death and provided names of several individuals whom he wanted authorities to examine.“I stated the facts exactly as they were; I told them everything that happened to my daughter. I listed all the names: Aditya, Sooraj Pancholi, Dino Morea, and the bodyguards. They noted everything down. They said they would take action based on what I told them; the proceedings would begin in a few days,” he said.“The truth cannot be defeated. God stands where the truth is; that is why justice will be served,” he added. Mumbai Police had earlier maintained, after its inquiry, that Salian had died by suicide.
Article Summary: The central bureau of investigation (cbi) on monday registered an fir in connection with the death of disha salian, the former manager of late actor sushant singh rajput. The bombay high court ordered a cbi investigation into salian’s death and criticised the mumbai police for failing to register an fir.

Article Title: UP assembly elections and fight for Muslim votes: Decoding SP, Congress's Owaisi problem
Article Text:
Owaisi faces his biggest test in UP.

"I am ready to join hands. I am ready to form an alliance. Today is the time to talk. Don't cry later after the elections are over. We don't want the BJP to come to power again.” Asaduddin Owaisi, AIMIM

AIMIM’s UP plans

The BJP would be smiling either way

Akhilesh Yadav and Owaisi have long competed in appeasement politics. Now they have set aside the contest over who will be the bigger 'bhaijaan' and are looking at a 'bhaijaan collaboration'. Owaisi is effectively sending Akhilesh ji a friend request. They are two sides of the same coin Asaduddin Owaisi, AIMIM

Catch-22 for opposition parties

That was Asaduddin Owaisi 's outreach-cum-warning to Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav in July at a rally in Moradabad while he launched AIMIM ’s campaign for the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections due early next year.Seeking alliance with opposition parties is now a part of Owaisi’s playbook to counter allegations of being a vote-cutter and the B-team of the BJP . We have seen AIMIM adopt similar strategy in other states like Maharashtra and Bihar. In both these states, it went all out to seek space in larger opposition alliances before deciding to contest on its own when its offer was rejected. Then the "rejection: became a part of Owaisi's campaign: we asked you to come in, you kept us out, so don't blame us for what happens next."So, when Owaisi reached out to Samajwadi Party in July, it was on expected lines and did not come as a surprise. But there is now a twist in the tale.Owaisi’s Uttar Pradesh plans suffered a jolt this month when one of his most trusted aides and the party’s national spokesperson Syed Asim Waqar dumped the party to join the Congress.Waqar, who rose to prominence defending the AIMIM and its politics, was a prominent voice for AIMIM in Uttar Pradesh and hence his crossing over to the Congress potentially impacts Owaisi's bid to make electoral inroads in UP.But more than his exit, it was his parting remarks that will bother Owaisi. “Being in the AIMIM for so many years, I felt that we pay lip service by stating that the BJP must be removed, but on the ground, we don't fight the BJP; we fight the Congress, the SP; we are fighting every other person who wants to remove the BJP,” Waqar said when asked about his decision to leave the AIMIM.Justifying his switch, Waqar said, “If we (AIMIM) keep fighting the opposition and do not allow it to blossom, then we are helping the BJP. I have decided that if we are true nationalists and want to remove the BJP honestly, then our objective should be to fight the BJP. If we are fighting the enemies of the BJP, then we are friends of the BJP. In reality, if someone is fighting the BJP across the country, it is Congress, Rahul Gandhi and his team. "Now, this is precisely the point which the opposition parties make against Owaisi and his AIMIM.Uttar Pradesh has been a difficult story for Owaisi. His AIMIM failed to win a single seat in the 2022 assembly elections in the state. And that makes the 2027 challenge a real test of whether the Bihar formula will work or whether Akhilesh is right to believe that AIMIM is a rival he can afford to ignore.Even while offering to join hands with Akhilesh, Owaisi chose to kick off AIMIM's 2027 campaign from Matera in Bahraich, a seat held by the Samajwadi Party. He also announced AIMIM’s candidate from the seat making his intent very clear.Owaisi questioned what SP leaders had done for the area despite getting Muslim votes, while saying AIMIM was ready for an alliance only if it was treated with 'respect' and given 'equal status'.The party has dropped enough signals to suggest that it is preparing for a much bigger push in UP in 2027. The party has also divided the state into zones and appointed regional in-charges as part of its attempt to strengthen the organisation before the election.AIMIM accepted that its performance was not up to the mark in 2022 but asserted that the party has spent the last few years trying to correct that.AIMIM's Uttar Pradesh president Shaukat Ali has said the party could contest around 200 seats if it fights alone. He has also kept the door open for a possible understanding with the BSP."Our natural alliance, if we were to forge one, would be with the BSP. Muslims and Dalits together account for nearly 40% of the vote share, enough to defeat both the SP and BJP," Ali said.The Samajwadi Party and the Congress will keep a close watch on AIMIM’s BSP outreach as it can have the potential to disrupt a lot of political calculations in the state. However, for now Mayawati has made it clear that her BSP will not forge any alliances with any party for elections.The 2027 assembly elections in UP is likely to see a very keen contest for Muslim votes. The switching of sides by Asim Waqar exposes the keen contest among the non-BJP parties for support of Muslims in the upcoming elections.The Congress, which would consider this AIMIM import as a big boost to its prospects, had contested the 2024 Lok Sabha elections in alliance with the Samajwadi Party, and, as of now, they are both part of INDIA bloc ahead of next year’s assembly elections.But this alliance has not stopped the two parties from taking measures to consolidate their individual support bases. Last month, the Samajwadi Party got a boost when the son-in-law of Congress MP from UP’s Saharanpur Imran Masood joined the party in the presence of Akhilesh Yadav. Imran Masood has been very vocal against SP and its chief Akhilesh Yadav accusing them of imposing as the ‘big-brother’ in SP-Congress alliance for the 2027 UP polls.For the SP, the Alpsankhyaks (read Muslims) form an important component of Akhilesh Yadav’s PDA outreach. In fact, his success in Uttar Pradesh till now has been largely powered by the Yadavs and the Muslims. And while, Akhilesh desperately tries to broaden his support base by reaching out to the Dalits, women and even the Pandits, he cannot make big gains without the support of Muslims.However, that does not stop the Congress from making its own outreach to the community in a bid to try and win them back. After all, for several decades the Muslims had contributed to the electoral success of the Congress. It was only with the rise of regional parties that they drifted away from the grand-old-party. So, it will naturally be happy with Asim Waqar on its side.The AIMIM, which is the third pole of Muslim politics in the state, will try to take advantage of the posturing and war of words between the two alliance partners as it tries to find its space in the state.AIMIM has shown that it can become a serious player where its support is concentrated. What it has not yet shown is that it can do the same in Uttar Pradesh, where the Samajwadi Party remains the main beneficiary of Muslim votes against the BJP.In the 2023 Telangana assembly election, the party contested nine seats and won seven, underlining how strong its hold remains in parts of the state.Bihar has been its most successful experiment outside Telangana till now. The party managed to win five seats in 2020 and repeated the number in 2025, mainly in the Seemanchal region.In Maharashtra, AIMIM has pockets of support but won just one assembly seat in 2024. In Uttar Pradesh, the challenge has been tougher. In the 2022 assembly election, AIMIM contested 96 seats but failed to win any. Its statewide vote share remained below 1%.Owaisi’s move to contest the Panchayat and Municipal body elections in Rajasthan shows the party’s intent to expand its base in states where it was not a player till now. The AIMIM chief maintains that the state needs a strong third political alternative apart from the ruling BJP and the Congress which have been the dominant players in state’s politics till now.In a bid to disturb the duoploy, Owaisi has announced that if Rashtriya Loktantrik Party chief Hanuman Beniwal emerges as a third force, the AIMIM will support him and work together to challenge both major political parties. Owaisi said, “Hanuman Beniwal and AIMIM together will make the lives of BJP and Congress leaders difficult.” He also appealed to voters to support AIMIM candidates and RLP candidates contesting elections on the party’s bottle symbol.While the Congress and the other opposition parties keep an eye on AIMIM’s political moves, the BJP perhaps would not be worried much.When Owaisi had reached out to Akhilesh, BJP wasted no time in mocking the proposal. Former BJP spokesperson Shehzad Poonawalla had then called it a 'friend request' to Akhilesh and accused both parties of vote-bank politics.For the BJP, Owaisi can be useful either way, more so in Uttar Pradesh.If AIMIM contests separately and takes away even a small number of votes from SP-Congress in close seats, the BJP may benefit. If AIMIM joins the alliance, the BJP can use Owaisi's presence to sharpen its attack on the opposition over minority appeasement.The opposition parties are reluctant to accept Owaisi’s offer to ensure that non-BJP votes, especially of the Muslims, do not split. They know that Owaisi’s offer is like a double-edged sword. Most of these opposition parties like the RJD in Bihar, Samajwadi Party in Uttar Pradesh have banked heavily on the support of Muslims for their politics. If they accept AIMIM as an ally, they fear losing the support of Muslims and this will eventually weaken their own minorities’ politics.Second, any opposition alliance with AIMIM will give the BJP a very strong weapon to engineer reverse polarisation. Since Owaisi is known for a very aggressive hardline brand of politics on issues concerning the minorities, the opposition will find it difficult to dissociate itself from the AIMIM. And this will give the BJP an opportunity to mobilise the Hindus against the opposition parties and eventually corner them.Clearly, the Samajwadi Party and the Congress have a Owaisi challenge at hand as they gear up for the 2027 challenge in Uttar Pradesh.
Article Summary: Owaisi faces his biggest test in up. "i am ready to join hands. Today is the time to talk. Don't cry later after the elections are over. We don't want the bjp to come to power again," he said. Aimim failed to win a single seat in the 2022 assembly elections in the state.

Article Title: Kejriwal-Sardesai Goa gambit: Attack defections, welcome rivals
Article Text:
The alliance has presented itself as a "non-BJP, non-Congress alternative".

Memory of 2017 and 2022

The 'open door' politics

The GFP complication

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Aam Aadmi Party and Goa Forward Party on Sunday announced a new political beginning for the state. They announced a pre-poll alliance for the upcoming 2027 assembly election named 'Goa First' and promised voters something the state has struggled to get: a mandate that actually stays intact.There was plenty of familiar political rhetoric at the launch in Panaji on Sunday. AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal claimed that BJP would not win a majority. "The people of Goa want a change. Goa First will form the government. We will win on our own," Kejriwal claimed.Both parties presented the alliance as a credible, "non-BJP, non-Congress alternative".In the press conference, the newly-formed alliance tried to build its political identity around a simple charge: defection.GFP chief Vijai Sardesai attacked the ruling establishment as a government of defectors. He said the BJP had not received a complete mandate in the previous elections and that even the Congress leadership could not deny the possibility of another round of defections.Kejriwal also opened up about the recent Rajya Sabha defection led by former blue-eyed boy Raghav Chadha. "It is a matter of great regret that our Rajya Sabha MPs left the party.They betrayed the party. The party sent them to the Rajya Sabha; the people did not send them," the AAP chief said.He said the AAP had never betrayed the people through its elected representatives."We believe that this is a lesson for us because such a thing has never happened in the Aam Aadmi Party before. From now onwards, before sending anyone to the Rajya Sabha, we will scrutinise the person thoroughly and ensure that he is the right person," Kejriwal said.However, after the story of 'Goa First' gets interesting, at its hard-launch itself.GFP chief Sardesai declared: "This alliance has not closed the door; it is open to the like-minded political forces. Many people have approached us, including leaders from both parties who are tired of their politics.The anti-defection pitch is not difficult to sell in Goa because voters have seen the numbers change dramatically after elections.In the 2017 assembly election, Congress emerged as the single-largest party with 17 of the 40 seats, while the BJP won 13. Yet Congress did not form the government. The BJP stitched together a coalition with regional parties and independents, with GFP chief Vijai Sardesai becoming deputy chief minister.Two years later, the picture changed again.In July 2019, 10 Congress MLAs joined BJP, taking the saffron party's strength to 27 and giving it a clear majority. The Congress, which had started the assembly term with 17 MLAs, was left with five.Then came the 2022 election.This time, BJP turned out to be the single largest party with 20 seats in the hung assembly. Congress won 11 and AAP two, while GFP won one. BJP formed the government with support from 2 independents and Maharashtrawadi Gomantak Party (MGP).Six months later, however, again eight of Congress's 11 MLAs joined BJP.Among them were former chief minister Digambar Kamat and then leader of opposition Michael Lobo. Congress was reduced to just three MLAs, while BJP's strength rose to 28.Defection runs so deep in Goa politics that, just eight months before the 2022 exodus, some Congress MLAs had gone to extraordinary lengths to prove they would stay put. They visited a temple, chapel and mosque, and signed affidavits promising not to defect. In September 2022, eight of the 11 Congress MLAs joined the BJP anyway.After years of battle in the assembly and courts, the Supreme Court in July had agreed to hear a plea challenging a decision of the Goa assembly speaker rejecting a petition by the Congress for disqualification of the eight MLAs.For Goa First, this history of defections may prove to be strong campaign material.Sardesai himself made clear that 'Goa First' is not going to be a closed club.The alliance, he said, was open to "like-minded political forces". He claimed that leaders from both major parties had already approached them because they were tired of their respective politics.Strategically, that makes perfect sense.AAP and GFP together currently have only three assembly seats. If the alliance wants to become a serious statewide force, it needs some established names and local networks. Goa's politics is intensely constituency-driven and established local faces can matter enormously.Turning away a strong BJP or Congress leader simply because that leader once belonged to the other camp could leave 'Goa First' with an admirable principle and a thin candidate list.But by welcoming such politicians, the alliance risks playing the very same game it accuses BJP of playing.However, if the leader joins before the elections, the alliance could defend it easily.There is another reason Sardesai's role makes this debate particularly interesting.GFP itself has travelled through Goa's shifting alliance landscape.In 2017, it was part of the BJP-led coalition that formed the government after Congress emerged as the largest party. By 2019, the relationship had broken down, and Sardesai became a bitter opponent of the BJP government. GFP subsequently allied with Congress for the 2022 election.It is now joining hands with AAP and positioning itself against both BJP and Congress for the 2027 elections. Thus, the positioning of the party has remained fluid.That, though, is not necessarily a contradiction, as we have seen several regional parties routinely negotiate their political space by switching alliances.The 'Goa First' alliance has now officially entered the 2027 Goa contest with defection as one of its central political themes. Yet, with its doors open to leaders from the BJP and Congress, the alliance's own composition could become part of the election narrative. The first real test of that balancing act will come with its candidate selection.
Article Summary: Aam aadmi party and goa forward party announce pre-poll alliance for 2027 assembly election named 'goa first' both parties present themselves as a credible, "non-bjp, non-congress alternative" the 'goa first' alliance has officially entered the 2027 goa contest with defection as one of its central political themes.

The 2028 challenge

NEW DELHI: The Rajasthan civic poll results have reinforced the dominance of the ruling BJP despite some setbacks, brought cheers to the AAP and the CPM, but has rung alarm bells for the Congress ahead of the 2028 assembly elections in the state.The BJP has lost some ground, but the Congress has not gained all of it. Parties like AAP and the CPM have sprung surprise in some districts at the expense of the Congress. The AAP has emerged the winner in Baran Nagar Parishad, while the CPM has gained majority in Nokha Nagar Palika.The ruling BJP led the Congress in the Rajasthan urban local body elections, winning over 4,179 wards against the opposition party's 3,613 as results for at least 10,200 wards were declared. Independents put up a strong performance across the state, winning 2,273 wards, emerging as a potentially decisive force in several urban bodies.In a post on X, PM Modi said the results reflected support for the BJP’s policies of development and good governance under the “double-engine government”.“Heartfelt thanks to the people of Rajasthan for delivering a resounding victory to the BJP in the municipal elections.This is a testament to the triumph of truth over the jhooth ki goonj (echo of lies),” PM Modi wrote.The results are a shot in the arm for chief minister Bhajan Lal Sharma. Sharma was picked up by the BJP to lead the Rajasthan government, ignoring the claims of heavyweights like Vasundhara Raje, after the party won the 2023 assembly elections against the Congress. The BJP would be happy that despite the loss of some ground, overall it has dominated across the state.The chief minister would especially be satisfied with the results as it comes in the backdrop of several controversies that had cropped up in the recent past. The NEET paper leak expose, the Karni Sena protest over UGC regulations and the CJP campaign against the state of government schools were some of the issues that had put the state government on the backfoot. But the results show that these issues may have had a limited impact on the party’s electoral prospects.Chief minister Bhajanlal Sharma thanked the voters for placing their trust in the party."Today, I express my sincere gratitude to the people of Rajasthan for the historic and magnificent victory achieved by the Bharatiya Janata Party in the state’s municipal body elections. I also thank all the party workers who dedicated their time and effort to secure this victory. I dedicate this triumph to them and to the people of Rajasthan, and offer them my congratulations and best wishes. The people of Rajasthan have endorsed the historic work accomplished in the state over the past two and a half years under the leadership of our Prime Minister Narendra Modi. They have embraced the Prime Minister’s vision of a ‘Viksit Bharat’ and a ‘Viksit Rajasthan,” he said.The CM also thanked the youth of Rajasthan for placing their trust in Prime Minister Narendra Modi and claimed that his government had, in the past two and a half years, fulfilled 78% of the pledges it made to the public.The Congress has also made significant gains in some key civic bodies, but the party should be worried about AAP and CPM entering the opposition space and making gains at its expense. The victory of AAP in Baran and CPM in Nokha should be warning bells for the Congress which has been the dominant challenger and only alternative to the ruling BJP.Reacting to the verdict, state Congress president Govind Singh Dotasra said, "When local elections happen, most votes tend to go in favour of the ruling power. This has been the trend for a long time. But this time, the BJP has been completely wiped out. In the Lok Sabha, more than 50% of their votes were there, and today they've dropped to within 34-35%.”Dostara accused the BJP of engaging in dishonest practices in the wards and delimitation.“In a major city like Jaipur, within the municipal corporation, Congress is ahead of the Bharatiya Janata Party in total votes by a margin of 10,000 votes. So, if we assess just the Jaipur Municipal Corporation, the BJP is behind Congress by 60-65 thousand votes. The vote percentage between Congress and the Bharatiya Janata Party—whenever the BJP was in power, it used to be around 9% ahead. Last time when we were in government, we were ahead by 2-2.5%. The misgovernance they've delivered, the public has shown them the mirror... In the 10 municipal corporations where the Chief Minister went, they managed a majority in only four, and that too due to dishonest delimitation; in the remaining 6, the majority is with Independents and Congress, not the Bharatiya Janata Party. This shows that this government has completely failed. Panchayat Raj elections are coming up, and in those, the Bharatiya Janata Party will face twice the debacle," the state Congress chief claimed.Dotasra also alleged that the Congress would have won around 1,500 more wards but for irregular and "unfair" delimitation of wards.He said the Congress won 542 wards reserved for Scheduled Castes, against 350 won by the BJP.In SC women-reserved wards, he said the Congress won 261 seats compared with 186 by the BJP, while in ST women-reserved wards, the Congress won 53 against the BJP's 39.Dotasra said the Congress won 37 of 80 wards in Ajmer, against 32 won by the BJP.The Congress registered a decisive victory in the Jhalawar Municipal Council, winning 18 of its 25 wards in a region considered a political stronghold of former Rajasthan chief minister and senior BJP leader Vasundhara Raje. BJP national vice president Vasundhara Raje is the sitting BJP MLA from Jhalrapatan assembly constituency of Jhalawar district. The district has a total of eight urban local bodies.The Congress also delivered a major blow to the BJP in the Pali Municipal Corporation, turning the party's traditional stronghold into a closely contested political battleground.Pali is the home district of Rajasthan BJP President Madan Rathore, who has served as the party's Pali district president several times and was a two-time MLA from Sumerpur.In a significant setback for the BJP, the Congress not only emerged as the single largest party in the 65-member Municipal Corporation but also defeated the BJP in Rathore's own ward.The AAP would be very happy with its victory in Baran. The party won 31 of the 60 wards, crossing the majority mark on its own. The Congress was a distant second with 18 wards and the BJP nine, while Independents secured two seats. The result will be a big boost for Arvind Kejriwal’s party given the fact that it has limited presence in the state.The independents have emerged as the key players in the board formation in several districts. There are several civic bodies where the BJP and the Congress will need the support of Independent councillors to ensure control. Overall, it has been a strong show by the Independents.The 2028 assembly elections are still over two years away and these results will form the basis for course corrections for all the key stakeholders. The BJP had won 115 seats with a vote share of 41.7%. The Congress claims that BJP’s Lok Sabha vote share fell 15 percentage points. This will be clear only after the final results and vote divisions are out.While the BJP will look to plug its weaknesses, the Congress will also go back to the drawing board and rework its strategy for the next state elections. In the 2023 assembly elections, the Congress had won 70 seats with a vote share of 39.58%. However, for now it has a bigger challenge at hand- to beat the BJP in wooing Independents where the party has emerged as the single largest party but could not gain majority.

Mixed bag for congress.decisive congress victory in vasundhara raje’s bastion.boost for aap. The victory of aap in baran and cpm in nokha should be warning bells for the congress.

NEW DELHI: BJP candidate Kailashchand in Rajasthan's urban local body elections found himself at the centre of attention after the results declared that he had received only one vote from the ward that he contested.Kailashchand contested from Ward 13 of the Parbatsar municipality in Didwana-Kuchaman district.According to the state election commission website, Congress candidate Hina Khanam won the ward with 376 votes, while Independent candidate Rashid Khan finished second with 195 votes.Kailashchand told news agency PTI that he was a voter in Ward 12, but the BJP fielded him from the neighbouring Ward 13."I got one vote. My vote is in Ward 12. I was fielded from Ward 13. Someone from that ward has voted for me," he said.The Parbatsar municipality has 25 wards, of which Congress won 13 and the BJP 12.Kailashchand's one-vote tally stood out as counting continued for 309 urban local bodies across Rajasthan.Rajasthan's urban local body election results threw up some strikingly low vote tallies, with a BJP and a Congress candidate securing just one vote each, while a Rashtriya Loktantrik Party (RLP) candidate drew a blank.The results came as counting was under way for elections to 309 urban local bodies across the state.More than 10,000 councillor posts were at stake in the elections.

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: More than 19,000 residential areas have set up community rooftop solar systems under PM Surya Ghar Yojana to power common utilities, benefiting over 9 lakh households.Officials said the clean energy generated is used for operating lifts, common-area lighting, water pumps, security systems and sewage treatment plants. Govt has released Rs 422 crore as central financial assistance to resident welfare associations (RWAs) to help them install the systems.“With common-area electricity bills forming a significant component of monthly maintenance expenses in many large housing complexes, govt support helps them reduce recurring costs while transitioning to cleaner energy,” an official said. The cumulative rooftop solar capacity of over 278 MW has been installed for these communities.Gujarat leads in total installations, with more than 9,000 housing societies setting up solar capacity, followed by Maharashtra, where over 7,500 residential areas have opted for the facility. Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka are also steadily expanding the adoption of community solar, said another official.Ahmedabad, Pune, Vadodara, Nashik and Surat are among the top five cities with the highest number of rooftop solar installations for housing societies.To make community-scale rooftop solar financially viable, govt provides central financial assistance of Rs 18,000 per kW for eligible RWA and group housing society projects. Housing societies in special category states and Union territories, including the North-Eastern states, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, and Lakshadweep, are eligible for a higher central financial assistance (CFA) of Rs 19,800 per kW, the official added.Launched in Feb 2024, PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana (PMSGMBY) aims to bring rooftop solar to one crore Indian homes by March 2027. The total number of rooftop solar installations, including individual households, has reached 47.8 lakh with total installed capacity of 16.8 GW, benefitting nearly 56.9 lakh families. The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy has so far disbursed over Rs 31,515 crore as central financial assistance, while several states are also running separate subsidy schemes to promote the installation of rooftop solar systems.

The clean energy generated is used for operating lifts, common-area lighting, water pumps, security systems and sewage treatment plants. Govt has released rs 422 crore as central financial assistance to resident welfare associations to help them install the systems.

NEW DELHI: The National Medical Commission (NMC) has sought a detailed report on allegations that a private medical college in Bihar made payment of a ₹3.75 lakh hostel fee mandatory for MBBS graduates to start their compulsory internship, with a July complaint alleging that interns feared they would be denied internship if they did not pay.The NMC has forwarded the complaint to the Bihar Directorate of Medical Education and sought a detailed report within 15 days. It has also asked the college to furnish its report on the allegations.The case involves R.D.J.M. Medical College & Hospital in Muzaffarpur, Bihar, where 2021-batch MBBS graduates allegedly faced restrictions on joining their Compulsory Rotatory Medical Internship (CRMI) unless they paid the hostel fee and stayed on campus.The issue was formally brought before the NMC on July 24 by the United Doctors Front (UDF), which represented the affected interns. The complaint alleged that students who had cleared their Final MBBS examination were being prevented from commencing internship and that some had already paid the hostel fee fearing they would otherwise be denied internship.Documents enclosed with the complaint include a July 18 college order stating that no student would be permitted to join MBBS internship unless the prescribed hostel fee was paid in full.The order further stated that, after verification of hostel-fee records, only one student was then eligible to join the internship, while other students would be permitted to join only after clearing their hostel dues.The UDF argued that the NMC's requirements provide for accommodation for students and interns but do not authorise a college to make hostel residence compulsory or withhold internship for non-payment of hostel fees.Dr. Lakshya Mittal of the UDF said, “medical students and interns cannot be treated as a source of forced revenue. If a student has fulfilled all academic requirements and is eligible to commence compulsory internship, imposing hostel residence and extracting lakhs of rupees as a precondition is a serious matter that requires regulatory scrutiny. We welcome the NMC’s intervention and expect the Bihar authorities to conduct a time-bound and transparent inquiry. ”
Article Summary: The case involves r.d.m. Medical college & hospital in muzaffarpur, bihar. 2021-batch mbbs graduates allegedly faced restrictions on joining their compulsory rotatory medical internship (crmi) unless they paid the hostel fee and stayed on campus.

NEW DELHI: Jammu and Kashmir Police on Monday busted an Over Ground Worker network allegedly linked with terrorist outfit Lashkar-e-Taiba and arrested three persons.According to officials, the accused were involved in providing logistical support, safe transit and other ground-level assistance to terrorists. They allegedly acted as guides and facilitated the movement of terrorist groups towards the Kashmir Valley.According to Rajouri Police, the individuals, identified as Zakir Husaain, Mohd Azam and Mohd Mustaq, are also suspected of having provided ground support to terrorists linked with multiple high-profile attacks, including an attack targeting civilians.During the course of the investigation, an IED was recovered based on the disclosure of one of the accused.A police spokesperson said that preliminary findings indicate that the device had allegedly been handed over to the accused by members of a terrorist group for safe custody and its possible use in a targeted attack.The police are continuing the investigation to establish the complete network, identify additional associates and ascertain the full extent of the accused persons' involvement, the spokesperson added.
